input.brief: ShilpSmith, a one-person 3D printing studio in Bareilly, India: personalised nameplates, Mini Me figurines, NFC smart idols, made to order, layer by layer

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Object splits the headline
hero.blueprint: One deep, flat ground colour. The object, a low-key studio photograph whose background matches the ground, stands at dead centre, scaled to 66% of the viewport height and tilted about 8 degrees, with its base cropped by the bottom edge. The headline is split around it: line one is centred across the object's upper fifth and line two across its lower fifth, both at clamp(64px, 5.8vw, 92px), regular weight, spanning columns 2–11, so the object fills the gap where a paragraph would normally sit. The type lies above the object in the stacking order in the light ink, so every letter stays readable where it crosses. At the object's mid-height two small text blocks at 14px face each other: the supporting sentence far left on columns 1–2, and two short facts (size, price) far right on columns 11–12, right-aligned, each 32px from its edge. Wordmark top-left; three text links top-centre; the single action top-right as a small light rectangular tab, the only light solid on the screen. The lower corners stay dark and empty.
hero.mobile: The object is 54svh tall, centred, its base cropped by the bottom edge. Line one of the headline crosses its top at 11vw and line two its lower third at 11vw, both centred inside 16px margins. The side text blocks merge into one 15px sentence under the navigation. Wordmark top-left and the action tab top-right; the links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: A two-line statement of four to six words, up to about 16 characters per line at 5.8vw, with the object standing between the lines.

type.note: A compact, warm grotesk set heavy with letters almost touching; small text stays in the same family at semibold. Suits music, events and culture pages where the type is the image.

palette.name: Orange and black
palette.note: Hot orange is the page: one flat field with blue-black type, flipping at a hard horizontal seam to a white section when the content needs a rest. The button is a solid block of the same blue-black with orange text, and every other colour comes from the objects shown.

photos.title: People
photos.note: figures, silhouettes and portraits, mostly unposed
photos.treatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Object in front of type
sections.blueprint: Type and object share one space instead of sitting side by side. Three or four lines of display type, one or two words each, are stacked flush left at clamp(72px, 9vw, 150px) with leading 0.88, starting on the left margin and allowed to leave the right edge (white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden on the section). The lines step through tones of one ink: one at 45%, one at full strength, the rest at 18%. The object photograph, a cut-out or a studio shot blended with multiply, is absolutely positioned over the upper right of the stack at 40–46vw wide, rotated no more than 6 degrees and above the type in the stacking order, so it hides parts of three or four letters. Under the stack, in columns 8–12, a two-paragraph block at 20px gives the facts. The full-strength line is the heading; nothing sits above it.
sections.mobile: Type drops to 15vw and still runs off the right edge. The object sits at 78vw wide, overlapping the last two lines from below instead of from the right, and is cropped by the right edge. The facts block follows at full width and 17px.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: One verb at a time
sections.blueprint: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it. In every panel a single word, the verb for that stage ('Cut', 'Fold', 'Stitch', 'Press'), is set at clamp(96px, 17vw, 300px), heavy and centred, inside a wrapper that is position: sticky; top: 50% and shifted up by half its own height. Because each word is sticky only within its own panel, it holds the centre of the screen while its photograph passes behind it, and is then pushed out by the next panel's verb. Use mix-blend-mode: difference in white, or one solid colour tested on every image. One sentence at 18px sits in the bottom-left corner of each panel over a neutral scrim limited to that corner. There is no separate heading: the verbs, read in order, are both the heading and the sequence.
sections.mobile: Panels stay 100svh, each photograph cropped to a vertical slice. The verb is 24vw, still sticky at the centre. The sentence sits along the bottom over a scrim at 16px, full width with 16px margins.

sections.name: Small frames, wide space
sections.blueprint: A flat, quiet viewport 100svh tall in which about 70% of the screen is empty. At mid-height a single row of small portrait frames runs across and off both sides: each frame 11vw wide and 24svh tall (roughly 2:3), spaced 5vw apart, vertically centred, six or seven visible at 1440. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border. The row scrolls sideways by drag or trackpad (`overflow-x: auto` with the scrollbar hidden) and may hold 12–24 frames. One line of text overlaps the top-left of the first frame by 12px: a title of two or three words at 20–24px followed by the count, placed above the frame in the stacking order. Hovering a frame scales it to 1.1 from its centre over 250ms; nothing else moves. No captions under frames, no arrows, and no other text in the section.
sections.mobile: The row sits at 45% of an 80svh section. Frames are 34vw wide at 2:3 and 5vw apart, so two and a half are visible and the row scrolls by touch with snapping. The title line sits 20px above the row at the left margin.

sections.name: Quotes in the gutters
sections.blueprint: A sticky stage (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`) inside a wrapper three or four viewports tall. The section's title, two or three words at 10–12vw, stays pinned across the top of the stage. In the centre a portrait photograph, 4:5 and about 30vw wide, changes at each scroll step. Each step also brings one quotation, placed in an outer gutter in a column 280px wide and at a different height each time: right gutter in the upper third, then left gutter at mid-height, then right gutter in the lower third. Quotations are bold at 22px with tight leading; the speaker's name follows at 15px in the softer ink. Only one quotation shows at a time. Each step may switch the stage to its own flat ground colour. Drive the steps with an IntersectionObserver on spacer blocks; never hijack the scroll.
sections.mobile: No pinning. The title sits once at 16vw. Each speaker then gets a block: the portrait at 72% width, flush left and flush right in turn, the quotation at 20px beneath it on the same edge, and the name under that. Leave 72px between blocks.

sections.name: Questions beside a tall photograph
sections.blueprint: One field in a deep or pale flat tone, split 5 to 7. Left, columns 1–5: a heading of two to four words at 36–44px; under it the three or four practical facts people ask first (address, times, how to arrive) as plain lines at 18px; then five or six questions as an accordion with no lines between rows, only 28px of space. Each question is a `<summary>` at 20px with a small chevron drawn from two 2px strokes at its right; the open answer sits beneath at 17px in the softer ink, on the same left edge. One filled button and one text link close the column. Right, columns 7–12: a tall photograph (3:4) that bleeds off the top edge of the section and stops 80px short of the bottom, with a second, square photograph a third of its width overlapping its lower-left corner by 40px.
sections.mobile: The tall photograph leads at full width, 4:5, with the square one overlapping its bottom-right corner at 38% width. Heading at 30px, facts at 17px, then the accordion at full width with 24px between questions and 44px touch targets. Button full width at the end.

sections.name: The object returns
sections.blueprint: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page. On one flat field 90svh tall, the object's photograph occupies columns 1–8, scaled to about 130% of that area and anchored so the section's bottom and left edges crop it (`overflow: hidden` on the section; on light fields `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes a white studio background). The text sits small in columns 10–12, vertically centred: a closing line of three to five words at 32–40px, one sentence at 17px, the price or key fact on its own line at 22px, and one rectangular button. Nothing overlaps the object's focal area. Where the page's subject is a shape rather than a photograph, the page's motif takes the object's place at the same scale as a flat filled shape. The closing line is the only heading.
sections.mobile: The text block comes first: closing line at 28px, sentence, fact, full-width button. The object follows at 130% of the screen width, shifted so the right and bottom edges crop it, filling about 55svh on the same flat field.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: starboy
references.idea: A tiny gadget shown enormous: product renders so large the screen crops them, wrapped around a nursery-rhyme headline in fat lowercase.
references.hero: No nav, logo or button. Off-white ground. The right half holds the headline: five stacked lines of very bold rounded lowercase at 13vw (187px), right-aligned and almost touching the right edge, with tight negative tracking and leading under 0.9, so the stack runs from 5% below the top to past the fold and the last line's descenders are cut off. The left 60% is one transparent-shelled, star-shaped device rendered at huge scale (yellow circuit board, round black screen), rotated and cropped by the top, left and bottom edges, its right-hand points tucking behind the letters. A chrome keyring loop peeks in at bottom-right.
references.type: Milling Triplex 1mm, bold, for the headline at 187px in lowercase with -0.055em tracking, one or two words per line over eleven lines; the same family at about 13px for body copy, product names and footer links, all lowercase. Two sizes only, a 14:1 jump.
references.colour: #f9f9f9 #2a2b2d #f5d900 #8d8e96 #b8a45c #2f6fe0 — Off-white page with charcoal type. Colour lives in the objects: circuit-board yellow, chrome, matte black, brass. A small blue logo in the footer is the only interface colour.
references.imagery: Photoreal renders of star-shaped devices in four materials, cut out with no background or cast shadow, scaled well beyond the viewport, each rotated differently and cropped by the edges. Accessories are shown small and centred in grid cells.
references.layout: Three acts: three screens of oversized renders tumbling diagonally with the headline set right, then left; one screen holding a single narrow text column and nothing else; then a three-column hairline-divided product grid running edge to edge with no outer margin.

sections.description: The second and third screens are only renders: a matte-black star and a chrome star overlap on a diagonal, each wider than half the viewport and cropped by two edges. The second half of the headline then appears left-aligned at the same 13vw, left of centre, while a brass star fills the right half and bleeds off the top and right. No captions or interface.

A single column of 13px lowercase text about 290px wide, placed roughly 15% from the left and starting at the top of the viewport: five short paragraphs, the first in medium weight. The remaining three-quarters of the screen is blank off-white. No heading, image or button accompanies it.

Three equal columns span the full viewport width, separated by faint 1px vertical and horizontal lines. Each cell holds one cut-out render centred with generous air and a caption row along its bottom edge: product name at left, price with stock count or a coming-soon note in grey at right, all 13px lowercase. The footer is one row: small blue logo left, five text links right.

steal: Scale the product until two or three viewport edges crop it, and let its silhouette tuck behind the headline letters.
Break a sentence into one or two words per line at 13vw, right-aligned for the first half and left-aligned for the second, so the headline spans several screens.
Follow a loud hero with one tiny text column on an otherwise empty screen; the drop in scale does the pacing.

references.name: Aevion
references.idea: One photoreal drone flies down the whole page through a white space organised only by hairlines and very light type.
references.hero: The first capture is the preloader: a white field with a tiny mono percentage counter dead centre. The loaded hero is white with a hairline-thin top bar: logo and a descriptor left, a credit and a live GMT clock in the middle, a small grey menu chip right. A pale blue-grey gradient panel fills the top 40% inside 12px margins. A white 3D drone hovers at centre, straddling a full-width hairline; a vertical hairline drops from it to the bottom edge. The headline is only 24px, two lines, far left, sitting on the horizontal rule with its second sentence greyed; a scroll cue sits far right on the same line.
references.type: Switzer in light weight (300) with -0.033em tracking for everything from the 24px headline to a single word at 16.7vw; protoMono at 12px in caps for bracketed labels and legal lines. Slate and pale grey mixed within one sentence. Four sizes.
references.colour: #fdfdfd #eef1f3 #24363f #a3abb0 #d5d9db — White on white with dark slate type and a paler grey for unrevealed words. The only tint is a faint blue-grey wash in the hero and the teal glint of the drone's lens. Cool.
references.imagery: A single white-and-grey quadcopter rendered live, with motion-blurred rotors, shown from front, three-quarter and side as it moves; often cropped by the right edge. Supporting graphics are hairline arcs and circles like a technical drawing.
references.layout: 12px page margins, content hung on a few full-width and half-width hairlines. Each screen holds one idea: a statement, a word, an object. Text stays left or lower-right while the drone travels between them. Nineteen screens of mostly white.

sections.description: White screen with a vertical hairline at 50% and a horizontal one near the bottom. Left half: a four-line statement at about 3vw in light grotesk, each word either dark slate or pale grey as a scroll-linked reveal passes through it. Right half: the drone in three-quarter view, cropped by the right edge and crossing the vertical rule.

A single noun set at 16.7vw in slate, top-left, the largest type on the page. A tiny mono label with a bullet sits far left at mid-height; a numbered chip sits top-right. The drone overlaps the right side at mid-height, and beneath it a 24px two-paragraph spec block occupies the right half, its later words still ghosted.

Landing diagram: the drone hovers above a drawing made only of hairlines: a large semicircular arc, a small circular target on the baseline, vertical dividers creating three bays, and a bracketed mono label above the target. Nothing else is on screen; the object and the drawing carry the whole frame.

Bracketed mono labels at both ends of a hairline, then a two-column row: a question at left, an answer plus a small square-cornered slate button at right. Below right, two short link lists in 12px; studio logo bottom-left; a mono legal line across the bottom edge.

steal: Use one hairline cross (a horizontal plus a vertical rule) as the only layout furniture and let the product render straddle it.
Set a single noun at 16vw as a chapter title and keep all explanatory copy at 24px, with nothing in between.
Reveal paragraphs word by word from pale grey to dark slate tied to scroll, so unread text stays visibly ghosted.
references.media: Every product view is real-time 3D: one fixed WebGL canvas carries the drone, centred at about 42% of the width inside an inset 1392x812 pale panel with a giant blurred wordmark behind it, then moves to the right half, then above a semicircle gauge, then inside a flat pale panel, while the HTML scrolls round it. The only photographic colour is one muted 8s clip filling the right half of a split.
references.motion: A numeric preloader counts for about 4.5s, then the page wipes up from the bottom by clip-path over 1670ms on a spring-shaped linear() ease, the ghost wordmark sharpens from a 200px blur over 2020ms, and the caption letters de-blur at a 50ms stagger. Lenis with two long pins (about 3.9 and 6.8 viewports) that step through three states each, swapping the drone's pose; statements scrub from grey to ink word by word, and buttons move over 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1).

references.name: Aardvark Book Club
references.idea: A book club dressed as a sweet shop: fat black type, tumbling 3D books and boxes on wavy colour fields, annotated with handwritten asides.
references.hero: A saturated yellow field with two large wavy blobs, pale yellow then orange, rising from the bottom. A three-line headline in Champ Bold, black, at about 8.3vw with leading under 0.85, is flush to a 15px left margin and reaches 60% across. Beneath it: a four-line paragraph 310px wide and a magenta split button (label plus arrow square). Right of centre a 3D hardback in navy and pink tilts 20 degrees, 600px tall; another book is cropped by the top-left corner, a third by the bottom edge. A purple handwritten note sits rotated at far right. Nav: pale-yellow pill links centred, an orange login button, black round social icons.
references.type: Champ Bold, an ultra-heavy wide sans with a looped g, for headings at 120px with tight tracking and leading; Degular for 18px body and pill labels; a purple handwritten script (Hello Organichand) for rotated margin notes and step labels. Three distinct voices.
references.colour: #ffd249 #faed8f #f9a21f #ffdbfd #a4f6f8 #fd48f2 — Each section owns one flat candy colour: yellow hero, white shelf, pink steps, cyan unboxing, deep violet footer. Type stays black; buttons are magenta.
references.imagery: 3D-rendered hardbacks and a patterned shipping box, cut out and tilted, floating over flat wavy vector shapes; real book covers on tilted coloured cards; black line drawings of figures on step cards. Nothing sits square to the grid.
references.layout: Sections are full-width panels with roughly 80px corner radius inset about 20px from the viewport, each a different colour. Headings alternate left and centre; cards overlap and rotate a few degrees; handwritten notes are tucked beside headings at an angle.

sections.description: White band. A centred black heading at 5.5vw over a two-line subline, with a rotated handwritten note at its upper left. Below, a horizontal row of book covers, each on a rounded colour-matched card with a small tag pill at top-left; cards tilt alternately by 3 degrees at staggered heights, the last cropped by the right edge, with two round arrow buttons above at right. Later, covers give way to same-coloured info cards with genre pills, heavy title and blurb.

A pale-pink rounded panel with lighter wavy shapes inside. Heavy black heading at left with a handwritten aside beside it; a small round logo stamp and a magenta split button at right. Along the bottom, four portrait cards about 250px wide in cyan, magenta, yellow and violet overlap like a fanned hand, each rotated a few degrees, with a handwritten step label at top, a black line drawing in the middle and a heavy caption at the foot.

A full-viewport cyan rounded panel containing only a 3D shipping box wrapped in a wavy magenta, violet and black pattern, centred. Across the scroll it goes from closed and tilted to lid open, growing to about 57% of the viewport width, with a single handwritten note at its right. No heading and no button.

The preceding white section ends in large rounded bottom corners over a deep violet footer. Left: white logo, two store badges, two magenta round social icons. Centre: the patterned box again, cropped by the bottom edge. Right: a small heavy heading, a white rounded email field and a magenta split button. A black legal strip closes the page.

steal: Give each section one flat saturated colour inside a large-radius inset panel and keep the type black across all of them.
Add rotated handwritten margin notes beside headings to carry secondary facts in a second voice.
Fan step cards so they overlap and tilt instead of sitting in an even grid.
references.media: About 60% of the first screen is picture: a 3D book and cropped book corners over a full-bleed illustrated wave field. Below come a sticky image-sequence of a box opening inside a rounded panel, a slider of tilted cards bleeding off the right edge, covers fanned like a hand of cards, a sticker collage round a circular badge and a cut-out box rising out of the footer: 37 images and two scroll-scrubbed canvases, no video.
references.motion: An indigo transition panel wipes away by 1.2s while the headline arrives word by word (515 split characters), and Lenis then drives the scrubbed scenes: the hero book turns through an image sequence, a sticky stage scrubs the box opening over 2745px, a headline slides along a curved path at scrub 0.5, and the footer is uncovered from under the rounded page. Buttons squash to 0.955 by 0.925 in 0.15s on press, the main ease is cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), and the bounce overshoots are ones the house motion layer does not use, though the site ships 32 reduced-motion rules.
